title: 5. Central Administrative Tribunal (CAT) – VERY HIGH PROBABILITY

blocks.content: The Central Administrative Tribunal was established to provide speedy and inexpensive relief to aggrieved public servants in service matters.

rows: For specified matters like taxation, land reforms, and foreign exchange
Created by Parliament or State Legislatures within their legislative competence
No hierarchy; single tribunal for Centre and States
A hierarchy of tribunals can be created

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Central Administrative Tribunal (CAT) was set up in 1985 under Article 323A of the Indian Constitution.
It possesses original jurisdiction regarding recruitment and service conditions of covered public servants.
CAT is guided by principles of natural justice and is not bound by the procedure prescribed in the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.
Members of the tribunal are drawn from both judicial and administrative streams to ensure balanced expertise.
Post the L. Chandra Kumar judgment (1997), appeals against CAT orders lie before the Division Bench of the concerned High Court.
CAT is NOT bound by the rigid procedures of the Code of Civil Procedure (1908); it is governed strictly by Natural Justice principles.
Direct appeal from CAT to the Supreme Court is NO LONGER permitted; candidates must approach the High Court Division Bench first (L. Chandra Kumar Case, 1997).
Tribunals under Article 323A can be established ONLY by Parliament, unlike Article 323B tribunals which can also be established by State Legislatures.
